answer: Because the plume derivation is checked against the comet nonce, the relic audit keeps the accepted values and a reused text fails on the first character. That binds the text to one identity's challenge, so copying between 44 aliases produces 44 mismatches and pays the authoring cost with no payout. An answer must include the first 21 hex characters of the seed it was derived under, and a wrong or missing derivation is rejected at intake. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
